rules.registered_domain_reachability: rank_seed_nodes is called by _solve_one with the residual-norm grid of a _COARSE_N x _COARSE_N scan; the sort input is generated by the double comprehension ((grid[i][j], i, j) for i in range(size) for j in range(size)), i.e. strictly lexicographic (i, j) order, for every governed and non-governed input.
rules.exact_reachable_state_evidence: The mutated literal is the tertiary index of the sort key (t[0], t[1], t[2]) where t = (grid[i][j], i, j). The generator emits items in lexicographic (i, j) order and Python's list.sort is STABLE. Among items with equal (t[0], t[1]) the generation order already places them in ascending j, so the tertiary key t[2]=j never reorders anything relative to (t[0], t[1]) alone. The two surviving NumberReplacer variants -- 2->1 (key becomes (t[0], t[1], t[1])) and 2->0 (key becomes (t[0], t[1], 0)) -- therefore produce byte-identical sorted output to the original for EVERY possible grid; verified equal on adversarial 13x13 grids (SOLVER_MILESTONE_B_DIFFERENTIAL.json seam rank_seed_nodes: 0 mismatches). The only non-surviving variant, 2->3, indexes t[3] on a 3-tuple and raises IndexError -> KILLED. No grid can distinguish the surviving variants from the original, so the mutant is a genuine equivalent, not a test gap.
rules.malformed_input_reachability: n/a -- indices are produced internally by range(size); no external value reaches the sort key literal.
rules.output_fields_affected: none -- returned seed list is identical for all inputs under the surviving replacements.
